primitives.name: Divider
primitives.useWhen: Separating content blocks with a full-width rule; optionally labelled with a short string.

props.label: string? — optional centred text label; omitting it renders a clean full-width rule

primitives.example: <Divider label="continued" />

primitives.name: DropCap
primitives.useWhen: Opening a long-form piece with an editorial drop-capital on the first paragraph.

props.children: ReactNode — wraps a paragraph; the CSS ::first-letter pseudo-element is applied to the first

primitives.example: A skin is not a theme file — it is an atmosphere.

primitives.name: Hero
primitives.useWhen: Opening a note or article page — sets the title, optional eyebrow label, and a lead hook sentence.

props.title: string — required; the primary headline
props.hook: ReactNode? — the 1–2 sentence stakes line below the title (canonical)
props.summary: ReactNode? — forgiving alias for hook; renders identically (hook wins if both set). Use either, never neither.
props.eyebrow: string? — small all-caps label above the title
props.frontmatter passthrough: source/commit/generated/type/status are accepted and ignored — the provenance strip renders them, not Hero.
props.children: ReactNode? — optional inline visual or decorative element

primitives.example:
<Hero
  eyebrow="Segment 03"
  title="The immersive layer"
  hook="Five coherent atmospheres, one token contract."
/>

primitives.name: Prose
primitives.useWhen: Wrapping free-form body text to apply --skin-measure width constraint and vertical rhythm.

props.children: ReactNode — any text content; headings, paragraphs, lists and blockquotes receive token-driven styles

primitives.example: A skin is not a theme file that swaps hex values.

primitives.name: PullQuote
primitives.useWhen: Surfacing a key insight or memorable phrase with typographic weight, distinct from an inline blockquote.

props.children: ReactNode — the quote text; displayed in a large display-font italic with an accent left-border

primitives.example:
<PullQuote>
  Radius, border weight, typeface personality, and shadow depth all move together.
</PullQuote>

primitives.name: Section
primitives.useWhen: Dividing a long note into named blocks with optional fractional markers (e.g. "02 / 07").

props.title: string? — section heading text
props.marker: string? — fractional label like "02 / 07" shown beside the title
props.icon: string? — any lucide kebab name; renders before the title to anchor the section. Choose by the section topic (e.g. "shield-check", "database", "list-checks").
props.animateTitle: boolean? — reveal the title word-by-word on scroll-enter (GSAP SplitReveal). Use on a marquee section or two, not every section.
props.children: ReactNode — section body content

primitives.example:
<Section marker="02 / 07" title="Token contract" icon="shield-check">
  Content goes here.
</Section>

primitives.name: Callout
primitives.useWhen: Drawing attention to a notable aside, warning, best-practice, or cautionary note inline with prose.

props.variant: 'info'|'warn'|'key-insight'|'pitfall'|'in-practice' — controls accent colour, default label, AND a default gutter icon (info/triangle-alert/lightbulb/octagon-alert/wrench); defaults to info
props.title: string? — override the auto-generated label
props.icon: string? — override the variant default gutter icon (any lucide kebab name)
props.children: ReactNode — callout body

primitives.example:
<Callout variant="key-insight">
  Selectors must return stable references — never project objects inside useShallow.
</Callout>

primitives.name: Card
primitives.useWhen: A single card cell inside a Cards grid; use h for a short heading and icon for a feature-grid glyph. Prefer giving every card in a grid an icon — they make the grid scannable and carry meaning at a glance.

props.icon: string? — any lucide kebab name; renders as an accent tile above the heading. Choose by meaning (e.g. "database", "shield", "rocket"). See the visuals-kit concept→icon table.
props.children: ReactNode — card body content

primitives.example: <Card h="Atomic SQL" icon="database">Single UPDATE … RETURNING; no read-modify-write race.</Card>

primitives.name: Cards
primitives.useWhen: Displaying a scannable grid of related items, each with an optional heading and body content.

props.children: ReactNode — one or more <Card> elements

primitives.example:
<Cards>
  <Card h="Performance">Token-driven shadow lifts on hover.</Card>
  <Card h="Tokens">Zero hardcoded values — all var(--skin-*).</Card>
</Cards>

primitives.name: Chip
primitives.useWhen: Inline status or classification badge; use tone to signal semantic meaning at a glance.

props.tone: 'program'|'debt'|'idea'|'done'|'next'|'risk'|'neutral' — controls colour palette; defaults to neutral
props.children: ReactNode — short label text

primitives.example: <Chip tone="done">Shipped</Chip>  <Chip tone="risk">Breaking change</Chip>

primitives.name: CodeBlock
primitives.useWhen: Displaying a multi-line code snippet with language label and a one-click clipboard copy button.

props.lang: string? — language label shown in the header (e.g. "tsx", "bash")
props.children: ReactNode — raw code string or pre-formatted content

primitives.example:
<CodeBlock lang="tsx">
  {codeString}
</CodeBlock>

primitives.name: Gist
primitives.useWhen: Surfacing the distilled takeaway of a section; wraps a <ul> of key points under a bulb icon.

props.children: ReactNode — typically a <ul> of concise bullet points (canonical)
props.items: optional ReactNode[] — forgiving alias for children; each renders as a bullet <li>. Use EITHER children OR items, never empty.

primitives.example:
• Selectors must return stable references.
  • Never project objects inside useShallow.

primitives.name: Ledger
primitives.useWhen: Listing tracked items with completion or risk status; rows carry icons that adapt across skins.

props.children: ReactNode — one or more <Row> elements (canonical)
props.items: optional { done?: boolean; risk?: boolean; title: ReactNode; sub?: ReactNode }[] — forgiving alias for children; renders the same <Row>s. Use EITHER children OR items, never empty.

primitives.example:
<Ledger>
  <Row done title="Shipped" sub="Merged to main 2026-06-20" />
  <Row risk title="Under review" sub="Awaiting adversarial sign-off" />
  <Row title="Next up" />
</Ledger>

primitives.name: Metric
primitives.useWhen: A single stat cell inside a Metrics row; value renders large, label renders small beneath.

props.label: string — descriptive label beneath the value
props.value: string — the headline number or string
props.icon: string? — any lucide kebab name; renders small above the value. Choose by what the metric counts (e.g. "git-branch" for threads, "database" for rows).
props.count: boolean? — count the value up from 0 on scroll-enter (GSAP). Safe on any value (non-numeric renders unchanged).

primitives.example: <Metric label="Token savings" value="87%" icon="trending-up" />

primitives.name: Metrics
primitives.useWhen: Displaying a row of key/value statistics or measurements with large display numerals.

props.children: ReactNode — one or more <Metric> elements (canonical)
props.items: optional { label: string; value: string }[] — forgiving alias for children; renders the same <Metric> cells. Use EITHER children OR items, never empty.

primitives.example:
<Metrics>
  <Metric label="Zones" value="42" />
  <Metric label="Coverage" value="100%" />
</Metrics>

primitives.name: Row
primitives.useWhen: A single row inside a Ledger; use done or risk to apply the matching icon and accent colour.

props.done: boolean? — renders a circle-check icon and muted/completed styling
props.risk: boolean? — renders the open-circle icon in the risk accent colour
props.title: ReactNode — primary row label
props.sub: ReactNode? — secondary line shown beneath the title

primitives.example: <Row done title="Auth shipped" sub="PR #42 merged" />

primitives.name: Timeline
primitives.useWhen: Rendering a vertical sequence of events or milestones connected by a dotted spine.

props.children: ReactNode — bare <li> elements; each becomes a timeline node (canonical)
props.items: optional ReactNode[] — forgiving alias for children; each becomes a node. Use EITHER children OR items, never empty.

primitives.example:
• Spec written + committed
  • Plan approved
  • Implementation shipped

primitives.name: Concept
primitives.useWhen: Marking a defined term inline so readers can link directly to it and hover to copy a deep-link to that specific concept.

props.id: string — anchor id; used as the fragment in the copied URL
props.children: ReactNode — the term text to display inline

primitives.example: The token contract governs all skin overrides.

primitives.name: Diagram
primitives.useWhen: Default-on: every digest gets ONE diagram of its core structure so a human grasps the note at a glance — flow / relationship map / hierarchy / lifecycle / decision split / before→after. Pick the angle that most clarifies; skip only when a note has nothing structural to draw (rare). The scene is authored via the Excalidraw MCP and saved to files/diagrams/. Fixed hand-drawn palette, same across all skins (not themed). See the excalidraw-diagrams skill for the authoring workflow.

props.src: string — visuals-relative path to the scene, e.g. "files/diagrams/render-loop.excalidraw"
props.caption: string? — short caption under the diagram

primitives.example: <Diagram src="files/diagrams/render-loop.excalidraw" caption="Script → Render pipeline" />

primitives.name: ReadingProgress
primitives.useWhen: Long-form articles or reference notes where showing scroll progress helps readers gauge depth and stay oriented.
primitives.example: <ReadingProgress />

primitives.name: StickyTOC
primitives.useWhen: Documents with multiple named sections where readers benefit from a persistent, active-highlighted navigation sidebar.

props.items: {id:string,label:string}[]? — explicit TOC entries; if omitted, derived from section[id] elements in the document on mount

primitives.example:
<StickyTOC />
// Or with explicit items:
<StickyTOC items={[
  { id: 'intro', label: 'Introduction' },
  { id: 'usage', label: 'Usage' },
]} />

primitives.name: Counter
primitives.useWhen: Count a number up from 0 on scroll-enter, preserving a symbol prefix/suffix ("~55", "100%", "18.45s", "~$0.50"). For stat rows prefer Metric count. Letter-led strings ("h264") render unchanged. GSAP — reduced-motion shows the final value immediately.

props.children: string — the final value, e.g. "100%" or "18.45s"

primitives.example: <Counter>18.45s</Counter>

primitives.name: Reveal
primitives.useWhen: Fading a block of content into view as the reader scrolls to it — headings, images, or any section that benefits from a subtle entrance.

props.y: number? — vertical offset in px to animate from; default 16
props.children: ReactNode — content to reveal

primitives.example: Section heading that fades in as you scroll

primitives.name: ScrollScene
primitives.useWhen: Wrap a section whose content should animate WITH scroll — scrubbed, optionally pinned. The cinematic storytelling block (GSAP ScrollTrigger). Reduced-motion → renders as a static section. Use sparingly: one or two per digest, on a section that rewards a beat.

props.children: ReactNode — the scene content (a single block: Cards, Diagram, Prose…)
props.pin: boolean? — pin the scene while a scrubbed timeline plays (implies scrub); default false. WARNING: pin RESERVES the pin scroll-distance (~80% vh) as empty layout space (a pin-spacer) → leaves a large gap around inline content. Only use for a full-viewport deliberate scene, never an inline diagram/cards in a reading flow.
props.scrub: boolean | number? — link the reveal to scroll progress; DEFAULT false = play once on enter (the reveal completes on its own; nothing stays stuck mid-scroll). Set true only for a deliberate scroll-linked scene.

primitives.example:
<ScrollScene effect="scale-in">
  <Cards>…</Cards>
</ScrollScene>

primitives.name: SplitReveal
primitives.useWhen: Reveal a short headline or emphasis line word-by-word (GSAP SplitText) on scroll-enter. For Section titles prefer Section animateTitle. Reduced-motion-safe (renders plain text). GSAP — see the gsap-* skills for idioms.

props.children: ReactNode — the text to split + reveal

primitives.example: <SplitReveal>Idea → Render in one loop</SplitReveal>

primitives.name: Stagger
primitives.useWhen: Animating a list of sibling items so they cascade into view one after another — cards, bullets, or any repeating block.

props.gap: number? — delay between each child animation start in seconds; default 0.1
props.children: ReactNode — sibling elements to stagger (array preferred)

primitives.example:
<Stagger gap={0.12}>
  <Card h="One">First card fades in.</Card>
  <Card h="Two">Second card follows.</Card>
  <Card h="Three">Third card last.</Card>
</Stagger>

primitives.name: Icon
primitives.useWhen: Inline glyph beside a label, card heading, list item or callout. Any lucide icon by kebab-case name; strokes inherit the skin colour automatically (currentColor) — never set a colour.

props.name: string — any lucide icon, kebab-case (e.g. "git-branch", "circle-check", "sparkles", "shield", "zap"). Legacy kit names ("bulb", "alert-triangle") still resolve. Recommended by use — status: circle-check/circle/triangle-alert/clock; nav: arrow-right/chevron-right/external-link; media: camera/image/film; data: layers/database/git-branch; emphasis: sparkles/zap/star/lightbulb.
props.size: number | string? — pixel/CSS size; omit to inherit the .skin-i default sizing

primitives.example:
<Icon name="git-branch" />
<Icon name="circle-check" className="skin-takeaways-icon" />

primitives.name: More
primitives.useWhen: A section has supplementary detail that most readers can skip — collapse it behind a disclosure trigger

props.summary: string — label shown on the trigger button (always visible)
props.children: ReactNode — the expanded content (hidden until opened)

primitives.example: Radix Collapsible under the hood — fully accessible, keyboard-navigable.

primitives.name: NoteLink
primitives.useWhen: A prose mention in the body references another note — turn it into navigation. Resolves ONLY against the source .md's own [[]] connections (it cannot invent an edge); the source must [[]]-link the target first.

props.to: string — the target note's bare slug as it appears in the source [[]] (alias/#heading/^block are stripped before matching)
props.variant: 'inline' (default, text link) | 'button' (compact pill CTA — keep the label SHORT, e.g. "View →"; long labels are ellipsis-capped)
props.children: ReactNode — the visible link text (short for the button variant)

primitives.example: <NoteLink to="2026-06-23-syndcast-skills-v1-design" variant="button">View →</NoteLink>

primitives.name: ReadingMode
primitives.useWhen: Mount once in the layout shell to give readers a Skim/Deep toggle — Skim hides any element marked data-reading-detail

primitives.name: Takeaways
primitives.useWhen: Place at the end of a Mind note as a completion ritual — summarises key points and links related documents

props.children: ReactNode — takeaway list items, use <li> elements (canonical)
props.items: optional ReactNode[] — forgiving alias for the children points; each renders as a <li>
props.related: optional ({ href: string; title: string } | string)[] — related docs in a grid below the list. A bare string is accepted (forgiving): a link-looking string becomes its own href, otherwise it renders as a label.

primitives.example:
• Payload auth guards /admin; Better Auth guards all frontend routes.
  • BA users sync to Payload via the afterOperation hook on login.
